title: Cross-Patient Pooling for Patient-Weighted While-Alive Estimands under Semi-Markov Recurrence
banked_reason: C-assumption-impractical: The load-bearing no-shared-frailty product restriction is justified only by an assertion that recurrence resets the disease clock, although shared patient severity commonly links recurrence and post-recurrence mortality.
gap_reasons: The load-bearing no-shared-frailty product restriction is justified only by an assertion that recurrence resets the disease clock, although shared patient severity commonly links recurrence and post-recurrence mortality; provide a defensible scientific design/regime justification or a dependence-robust sensitivity/attainability result.
proof_attempt_summary: Seven proposal revisions pursued an n^-1 minimax theorem using cross-patient pooling. The repair from fixed-horizon marks to common-duration follow-up addressed observation-induced dependence, but the estimator still requires latent recurrence-gap independence; without it, pairing targets a product-margin surrogate instead of the while-alive mean. A dependence-sensitive theorem would require a new proof spine and a new run.
tldr: For the identity patient-weighted while-alive mean, every recurrent participant is followed for a common duration \(H\) after recurrence, through calendar time at most \(H+\rho\). A homogeneous latent post-recurrence lifetime law without shared frailty makes recurrence time independent of the observed common-gap mark \(W_a\), although it does not make the ordinary baseline-horizon mark independent. Pairing recurrence times with other patients' common-gap marks, clipping the inverse-sum kernel at \(n\), and multiplying by the empirical recurrence fraction yields uniform MSE of order \(n^{-1}\), including \(\gamma=0\) and triangular exponents, with a matching same-class lower bound and a fixed-law Gaussian limit. Restricted-model efficiency remains open.
gap: Published patient-weighted while-alive analysis derives one-history influence-function estimators but does not establish boundary-uniform quadratic risk for a shared latent-gap reconstruction under common-duration post-recurrence ascertainment. General higher-order influence-function theory does not supply the observation map, product representation, survivor atom, projection moments, or same-class lower perturbation.
fill: The project establishes the observation map, exact latent-gap product representation, selection-corrected clipped cross-patient estimator, uniform \(n^{-1}\) upper and lower MSE bounds over the maintained class, and a fixed-law influence-function limit. The observation requirement and no-shared-frailty restriction remain explicit, and restricted-model efficiency is an open question.
